G01.notes: Three explicit learning goals connect the recorded design, retained count/volume, two concept checks and original mechanism/limit explanations. Navigation does not infer mastery.

G02.notes: One run per distinct liquid; first three individual drops demonstrate growth, optional five-drop additions reduce repeated motions. Drops are not independent trials and repeatability requires independent runs.

G03.notes: ACS institutional teaching sources support molecular attraction, water domes and surfactant effects. Water stays H2O; surface tension is not a solid skin. Exact virtual thresholds/doses are synthetic and are not attributed to empirical sources.

G04.notes: Limits are beside the bench and in reports/handouts: indirect count comparison, synthetic values, enlarged art, fluid simplifications, real confounds and limited repeatability.

G05.notes: Students clean the actual coin, place a dedicated dropper at the coin, add drops and see the dome/spill, then interpret counts and calculate retained volume. Correcting the spilling-drop error changes recorded evidence.

G06.notes: Inspected initial/residue, cleaned/growing dome and spilled states at desktop and phone/tablet. Coin, glass dropper and transparent fluid look plausible at declared scale. Compact frame and target percentages share the same coordinates and pass drag/scroll/resize/reload checks.

G07.notes: Concept and tool ordering is stable per attempt and does not reveal correct concepts. Scientifically meaningful liquid identity, equal drop size and observation order are retained.

G08.notes: Reviewed the full authored pathway, errors, checks, reports and handouts for ninth-grade wording. Cohesion, surface tension, polarity, hydrogen bonds, surfactant and retained amounts are defined. Teacher/student comprehension stays pending.

G09.notes: Required written prediction/design gate setup in both model and UI. First plan is retained before apparatus/results. Reasoned predictions can be wrong; no later outcome is shown before planning.
